headline: Revenue and profit accelerate on fuel-price tailwinds
summary_short: WEX posted Q2 2026 revenue of $753.6M (+14.3% y/y) and diluted EPS of $3.11 (+57.1% y/y), as segment margins expanded on elevated U.S. fuel prices and net income rose 59.3% y/y to $108.5M.
summary_long: Revenue rose 14.3% y/y to $753.6M, driven by higher payment-processing and finance-fee revenue in Mobility on elevated U.S. fuel prices, plus growth in Benefits (HSA deposits) and Corporate Payments (network incentives). Margins expanded across all three segments -- Mobility's adjusted operating margin rose to 43.2% from 38.7% as fuel-price gains outpaced largely fixed costs, partly offset by a higher credit-loss provision. Net income climbed 59.3% y/y to $108.5M and diluted EPS rose to $3.11 from $1.98. Cash and equivalents rose to $1,161.5M; the board authorized a new $1.0B buyback program, with $940.0M remaining. No forward guidance was given in the 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Mobility revenue rose on higher payment-processing and finance-fee revenue tied to elevated U.S. fuel prices; Benefits grew on higher HSA deposit balances; Corporate Payments grew on higher network incentives.

Mobility and Corporate Payments margins expanded as fuel-price gains and reduced collection risk outpaced largely fixed costs, partly offset by a higher Mobility credit-loss provision and increased G&A/stock comp.
Higher net income combined with a roughly flat diluted share count (34.9M vs 34.4M) drove diluted EPS growth.
Financing cash flow rose on higher net funding activity (deposits and FHLB borrowings tied to receivables funding), outweighing investing outflows and buybacks.
Consolidated profit growth is the sum of margin expansion in all three segments, each individually disclosed above; no single overriding cause was cited release-wide.
